messages:
maria: Quick sync 11 we need a practical stance on REST vs gRPC for internal model routing. Key constraints: client ergonomics, deterministic quotas, and console-friendly telemetry. Opinions?

ali: If we pick pure gRPC we get strong typing and easy bucketing for quotas, but browser teams will whine. Hybrid seems inevitable.

jon: Hybrid + small gateway to normalize sounds best. Gateway validates/enriches then forwards to runtime RPC. Keeps runtime simple.

nina: Agree. Gateway should stamp `x-rd-route-id`, `x-rd-trace-id`, `x-rd-sample-level`. Enforce schema derived from canonical proto.

maria: Sampling controls must be per-route in console (pct + conditional rules). Also payload-level capture needs strict ACLs.

ali: For quotas: use deterministic hash(tenant+route) in both gateway and runtime (doc algorithm). Emit `x-rd-quota-token` for diagnostics.

jon: Rollouts: console shows unified logical route (both REST & gRPC) with traffic split and quality regression alerts tied to prompt-tests. Auto-rollbacks on threshold.

deploy-bot: Canary job queued for gateway-admit-spike at 1759001140.

maria: Action: platform publishes proto + JSON schema; eng spike for gateway normalization; console wireframe for sampling/quota UI. I'll write up RFC tomorrow.
